reflection.summary: L002 executed successfully and passed the fixed G01 positive-Tc guard (8.5449 K <= 8.8322 K), but it did not improve the A05 incumbent. Pooled weighted OOF MAE was 7.8018 K versus 7.7526 K, a deterioration of 0.0492 K. Relative to A05, positive-Tc MAE worsened from 8.5051 K to 8.5449 K and reported-zero MAE worsened from 6.0806 K to 6.1508 K. High-Tc MAE improved slightly from 28.8502 K to 28.7654 K, showing a subgroup tradeoff rather than an eligible pooled win. On fe_anion specifically, hist_gradient_boosting/raw improved positive-Tc and high-Tc errors but worsened overall and reported-zero errors; the latter costs outweighed the gains. Thus neither a specialized hist_gradient_boosting/raw fe_anion expert nor the previously tested broad hist-gradient fallback improves A05.
reflection.next_focus: Retain A05 as the best guard-eligible development configuration: composition input, chemistry routing, extra_trees/raw global model, and extra_trees/raw experts for cu_o and other with fe_anion falling back globally. Any future work should evaluate A05 on a separately designed holdout or new data and, if development resumes, focus on richer ways to resolve the persistent cu_o zero-versus-high-Tc ambiguity rather than further combinations from this exhausted fixed menu.
